item.title: China, US maintain close communication on tariff reduction arrangement
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
China and the United States are maintaining close communication on implementing a reciprocal tariff-reduction framework that would cover $30 billion worth of products from each side, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday.
He Yadong, the ministry's spokesperson, made the remarks at a regular press conference, saying the arrangement would help stabilize and expand bilateral trade and had raised high expectations among business communities in both countries.
He expressed hope that the two sides would work together to advance the implementation of the arrangement at an early date and create more favorable conditions for bilateral agricultural trade.
China and the United States are maintaining close communication on their respective concerns regarding trade and investment, He said, adding that progress will be announced in due course.

item.title: Technology reshapes China's agricultural modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Guests communicate at the 38th episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency. (Xinhua/Sun Ruibo)
* China's autumn grain harvest has withstood the test of disasters this year, with more than 90 percent of the crop gathered by early November and full-year output expected to exceed 700 million tonnes for a third consecutive year.
* Technology has carried more of the load. Recent years have seen sustained efforts to raise per-unit yields through integrating improved farmland, seed, machinery and methods, with techniques such as rational close planting, precision sowing and integrated water-fertilizer irrigation.
* More than 95 percent of villages have 5G coverage, rural internet penetration has reached 69.5 percent, and the share of farming guided by digital information is rising about 2 percentage points a year in China.
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China's autumn grain harvest has withstood the test of disasters this year, with more than 90 percent of the crop gathered by early November and full-year output expected to exceed 700 million tonnes for a third consecutive year.
That was the assessment delivered on the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency, where guests discussed how technology is changing not just how much China farms, but how it farms.
HARVESTS WITHSTANDING DISASTERS
"Nationwide, autumn grain production has withstood the test of disasters, the overall situation is fairly good, and the foundation for a good harvest is solid," said Zhao Changbao, director of the Rural Economy Research Center of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs.
The approach to disasters has shifted, he noted. Rather than responding after damage occurs, agricultural departments moved work ahead of the weather, organizing a 100-day campaign to strengthen field management and combat disasters, and holding regular consultations with meteorological, water resources and emergency management authorities.
Northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, the country's largest grain producer, has maintained output above 80 million tonnes for two successive years and expects a record harvest this year, said Zhu Huasheng, deputy director of the province's agriculture department.
This province has developed 125 million mu (about 8.3 million hectares) of high-standard farmland, achieved near-full coverage of improved seed, and reached a mechanization rate of 99.34 percent for ploughing, sowing and harvesting, with 88,000 new types of agricultural business entities bringing smallholders into the effort.
In Dongjiao Village, in the central Chinese province of Hubei, meanwhile, where villagers once suffered from acute drought, ponds and embankments have improved water management efforts, while a heat-tolerant, lodging-resistant rice variety yielded more than 13.5 tonnes per hectare this year, said Hu Aiguo, Party secretary of the village.
Mechanization and specialized services have also helped cut losses. In north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, more than 19,000 farm machines and 1,710 service providers were deployed for the autumn harvest this year.
"Agricultural production is shifting from a single focus on raising field yields to raising yields, cutting losses and improving quality at the same time," Zhao said.
Plant protection drones carry out spraying operation on an intelligent farm in Liucheng Town of Dongyuan County, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Deng Hua)
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AS SUPPORT
The change starts at the seed. In Wuchang, a rice-growing county in Heilongjiang known for its premium rice, a scan of the code on a bag traces where the seed was sown, how the field was managed and when the grain was milled.
Local firms have worked with the Chinese Academy of Sciences to purify and rejuvenate Daohuaxiang No. 2, the variety behind Wuchang's reputation, and have built breeding centers, a 333-hectare propagation base and a multiplication base in south China's Hainan Province.
Machinery carries this change into the field. China's first tractor rolled off the line in 1958, ending the era of farming behind oxen. First Tractor Company Limited, a leading agricultural machinery provider, now builds 320-450 horsepower tractors with continuously variable transmission, and its Dongfanghong tractors hold straight-line accuracy within 2.5 centimeters using BeiDou positioning.
In October, this company, notably, unveiled an onboard AI agent at an agricultural machinery exhibition in north China's Tianjin that advises operators as they work.
"Domestic smart machinery makes sowing faster and more precise," said Wang Dongqing, deputy chief engineer of First Tractor. Mechanization, he added, is the link that connects people, machines, land and services.
Digital tools are spreading at the same time. "In the past we farmed largely by watching the sky, the land and our experience," Zhao said. "What is changing now is that we are starting to watch data, algorithms and screens."
The country's "No. 1 central document" for 2026 calls for integrating AI with agricultural development, and an action plan for 2026-2030 sets smart farms, intelligent breeding and AI application scenarios as priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030).
"Digital villages and AI are no longer an optional question," Zhao said. "They are a required one for agricultural modernization."
In Dongjiao, young people who returned from cities now use smart machinery and sensor networks, and grain growers have formed cooperatives to grow organic rapeseed for premium buyers.
"Village development depends on young people putting down roots," Hu said. Zhao stressed wider channels for bringing talent to villages, more concrete services for keeping them, and a thicker foundation for training local farmers.
Workers operate agricultural machines at a farm under the Beidahuang Group in northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, Oct. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Wanping/Xinhua)
INTEGRATION FOR DEVELOPMENT
Technology's effect on incomes is clearest where it meets the market. Heilongjiang has built a provincial brand for black-soil produce and promotes contract farming under which buyers order before planting. "In the past we planted whatever we could and then looked for buyers," Zhu said. "Now we plant what has been ordered."
Dongjiao has established 67 hectares each of cropland, peach orchards and fish ponds, and has also developed its rural tourism. Per capita income in the village reached 30,123 yuan (roughly 4,484.32 U.S. dollars) last year.
An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 7, 2026 shows students watching a harvester equipped with BeiDou Navigation Satellite System automatically harvesting rice in the field during an open class on smart agricultural machinery in Chongqing, southwest China. (Xinhua/Tang Yi)
"Goods that used to be sold by the basket at low prices are now sold by the box or by the piece, at several times the old price," Zhao said, crediting livestreaming, e-commerce and branding.
Wang said the next five years are both an opportunity and a responsibility for farm machinery makers, and that First Tractor will help rural young people use machinery as a platform for starting businesses.
For a country producing around 700 million tonnes of grain a year on a fixed land base, the key, as Zhao put it, is "putting technology into real agricultural production scenarios," as technologies are speeding up the modernization of agriculture and rural areas.

item.title: Danish business leaders, former diplomats see opportunities in China's 15th Five-Year Plan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Panelists take part in a discussion during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua)
COPENHAGEN, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Danish business leaders and former diplomats have said that China's 15th Five-Year Plan could open up new opportunities for economic cooperation between Denmark and China in areas such as wind power, pharmaceuticals and green shipping.
They made these remarks at panel discussions on China's latest five-year blueprint and the China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, on Wednesday.
Former Danish Ambassador to China Friis Arne Petersen said the plan covered a wide range of industries where the two countries could work together if policy conditions allowed.
Petersen said China's push to develop new quality productive forces, including through advances in artificial intelligence, could shape future cooperation in industry, agriculture, environmental protection and energy. He pointed to pharmaceuticals as an area where Danish companies could work with Chinese partners on research, manufacturing and sales.
Ove Ullerup, a former Danish diplomat and chairman of the board of Asia House, an association which works to strengthen ties between Denmark and Asia, said China's green transition targets could open up new areas of cooperation with Denmark. He noted that the two countries established a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2008 and launched a joint green work program in 2023.
Peter Dige Thagesen, head of geopolitics at the Confederation of Danish Industry, said Denmark's strengths in wind power, electricity and green technology align with China's priorities, and cooperation opportunities also exist in life sciences, food production and green shipping.
Thagesen said a survey of the confederation's members showed that Danish companies wanted to maintain trade with China while reducing dependence in critical areas.
Hans Henrik Pontoppidan, secretary-general of the Danish-Chinese Business Forum, said Danish companies should consider new ways to work with Chinese partners on research and development, particularly in health care.
Chinese Ambassador to Denmark Wang Xuefeng said the five-year blueprint has highlighted advances in science and technology, the green transition and further opening up, which would create more opportunities for Denmark and other partners.
The event was jointly organized by the Chinese Embassy in Denmark, the Danish-Chinese Business Forum and Asia House.
Attendees listen to remarks during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua)

item.title: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- In persevering with full and rigorous self-governance, the Communist Party of China (CPC) highlighted efforts to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm in tackling challenges.
How will the CPC deliver on this commitment? At the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in October, the CPC leadership sent the signal -- equally important to full and rigorous self-governance is how to encourage Party members and officials to better fulfill their duties, take on new challenges and tackle them.
The focus of efforts has been set on creating a clean and enabling political environment.
But the drive to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm doesn't stop here. In an enabling political environment, the next thing they need to better serve the people is competence.
Currently, the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century, and China is at a critical moment when the foundation for basically realizing socialist modernization needs to be consolidated and all-out efforts should be made to advance the cause.
It is more imperative than ever before to improve the competence of officials.
Officials need to develop their abilities to advance high-quality development, serve the people, forestall and defuse risks, and apply law-based thinking and approaches in their work.
For this purpose, they are encouraged to work at the primary level, keep abreast of new technologies, new industries and new business models, and learn the latest knowledge and expertise required for the fulfillment of duties.
The composition of the CPC membership has changed, with officials born after China's reform and opening-up in 1978 taking up an increasingly large share.
The healthy career growth of those officials has been highlighted on the agenda of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance.
The CPC creates opportunities for them to build up their skills and abilities in practice, whether on the front line of reform, development and stability endeavors, in major tasks, or in challenging but key positions.
Targeted training programs revolving around social and economic development goals during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) have been planned to help young officials close the knowledge gap and shore up their weaknesses in fulfilling duties.
The CPC also pledged to unequivocally support and speak up for those who assume responsibility and do solid work, particularly when they encounter setbacks or criticisms because of their bold and proactive moves in performing duties, or when they suffer from injustice because of misunderstanding or false accusations.
The original aspiration and mission of the CPC are to seek happiness for the Chinese people, and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
The CPC understands that the political ideal of serving the people and good governance cannot be achieved if pursuing power for power's sake or personal benefits becomes the ultimate goal of governance.
That's why the CPC has been taking a tough stance against corruption particularly since 2012, and why it places such great importance on building a clean political environment and a contingent of capable officials.
Governing the Party with strict discipline, the CPC is protecting the level playing field and stimulating positive energy for shouldering responsibilities. In this sense, such a Party self-governance endeavor bolsters economic and social development, and ultimately the wellbeing of the people.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as NVIDIA CEO, Colette Kress takes over
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO of NVIDIA. /VCG
Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately, NVIDIA's Board of Directors announced on Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO as the board begins searching for a permanent successor.
Kress will continue to serve as executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO. The board said it would consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent chief executive.
Kress joined NVIDIA in September 2013 and has served as executive vice president and CFO since then, leading the company's finance organization and playing a key role in its growth and development. Before joining NVIDIA, she spent nearly 25 years in finance positions at major technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.
Harvey Jones, chair of NVIDIA's board, said Kress had helped lead the company through a period of extraordinary growth and had a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.
The board expressed confidence in Kress and the company's leadership team, saying operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap were expected to continue without interruption.
Kress said she is committed to building on the foundation Huang had established over the past 33 years, advancing NVIDIA's work in accelerated computing and artificial intelligence, and serving its customers, partners, developers and shareholders.

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday.
The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said.
The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech.
President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.

item.title: China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
A gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Haitao)
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday held a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addressed the gathering.
Also present at the event were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee.
More than a century ago, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He died in 1925.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addresses a gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.
Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925.
Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event.
Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started.
In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution.
He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun.
For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said.
"The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said.
Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China.
He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly.
On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed.
Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times.
Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development.
"We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said.
Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation.
Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
"Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said.
Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed.
People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said.
"On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said.
"We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form."
"The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said.
A gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the gathering here on Thursday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)

item.title: How China is rebuilding 3,000-year-old bronze treasures
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
How do you put ancient treasures back together after thousands of years? At China's Sanxingdui archaeological site, conservators combine meticulous hands-on restoration with 3D scanning and digital modeling to study broken bronze artifacts and help reveal the extraordinary craftsmanship of ancient Shu civilization.
